newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium to host landmine ban treaty conference.
newsitem.headline: Belgium to host landmine ban treaty conference.

text.p: Belgium will host an international conference in June aimed at finalising a global treaty banning anti-personnel mines, the foreign ministry said on Wednesday.

More than 50 nations are expected to take part in the June 24 to 27 talks, which follow a similar meeting in Ottawa, Canada, last October. The Ottawa meeting committed the countries to working towards a ban, but did not lay down a timetable.
The foreign ministry said the first two days of the meeting would be spent drawing up a convention making a landmine ban legally binding.

The last two days would take the form of a debate, chaired by Belgian Foreign Minister Erik Derycke, on progress so far towards such a convention, regional initiatives against the use of anti-personnel mines and how to provide demining and other assistance to countries and victims.
A foreign ministry spokesman said it was too early to comment on whether large nations, such as Russia, which did not sign the Ottawa agreement, would take part.
In March 1995, Belgium became the first country in the world to adopt legislation prohibiting anti-personnel mines, the foreign ministry said.
